artifacts.summary: 7-phase plan in 4 waves (~7.75h): reserved-sentinel whole-tree-claim admission dimension (Part A) and plan-cache write-guard plus force-phases cache key (Part B).

memory_candidates.content: An implicit whole-scope claim that exists only in a deliverable's content (e.g. a plan phase invoking whole-tree regeneration) is structurally invisible to any admission gate built on intersecting DECLARED scope sets -- two actors can be mutually exclusive in practice while perfectly disjoint on paper. The durable fix is a RESERVED SLASHLESS SENTINEL token in the declared-scope array rather than a real wide path: a slashless token is inert in a directory-prefix overlap predicate (no exact match, no X/ prefix relation against any real path) and inert in the sibling containment predicate (nothing is ever under TOKEN/), so it adds detection without loosening any permissive scope check that consumes the same field, and it can be adopted by producers BEFORE the gate that reads it ships -- no backfill migration. A real wide path sentinel instead fails three ways: it inherits no phase-level exemption unless the consuming branch already reads a phase map, it trips coarse-declaration lints that exist to flag whole-directory-root entries, and it maximally loosens every containment consumer of the same field. Consume it as a NEW dimension appended LAST, evaluated only on a candidate the existing branches would otherwise admit, so non-regression of the existing branches is structural rather than tested.
